body:
Minutes:

- TPAC Agenda Preparation: Johnny Stenback opened the meeting by calling for contributions to the WHATNOT meeting agenda at TAC, noting that tracking would be handled through Anna's original [issue](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/issues/398). Johnny Stenback asked participants to provide suggestions and feedback either via comments on the issue or through direct notes.
- Meeting Schedule Adjustments: Philip Jägenstedt summarized feedback from the European-friendly meeting, noting a strong preference for a bi-weekly cadence due to time zone fatigue and the presence of European editors representing Blink, Gecko, and WebKit. Noam Rosenthal highlighted that end-of-day times are difficult for European participants who are heavily committed to American time zone calls. After discussing potential bottlenecks and the pros and cons of scheduling extra meetings, the group reached a consensus to trial an alternating bi-weekly schedule. Johnny Stenback and Philip Jägenstedt agreed to coordinate the exact week offsets with Nandu, dropping the meeting the week after TAC and starting the new setup thereafter. Additionally, Philip Jägenstedt and Anne van Kesteren noted that review backlogs are primarily driven by bandwidth issues on GitHub rather than meeting frequency, suggesting that more support for HTML spec reviews is needed.
- Custom Elements Callbacks and Parser State: Keith Cirkel raised issue 662 regarding developer requests for a mechanism to determine when the parser has finished populating children into an observed node, citing use cases such as JavaScript and markdown parsing ([00:11:12](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ZA1AKDb9YoXD6dFgLTegj2YPUyCWmq2vbJNvyotPrQU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-aWlRM8Z_eVAXtOStBeIwCQ&tab=t.9nfap4e7n9e6#heading=h.50dxmddqmkli)). While Anne van Kesteren objected in earlier discussions due to potential synchronization and document write concerns, Olli Pettay noted that main-thread performance impacts are minimal since op codes are handled directly on the main thread ([00:12:27](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ZA1AKDb9YoXD6dFgLTegj2YPUyCWmq2vbJNvyotPrQU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-aWlRM8Z_eVAXtOStBeIwCQ&tab=t.9nfap4e7n9e6#heading=h.50nyfarjxf1i)) ([00:15:03](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ZA1AKDb9YoXD6dFgLTegj2YPUyCWmq2vbJNvyotPrQU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-aWlRM8Z_eVAXtOStBeIwCQ&tab=t.9nfap4e7n9e6#heading=h.pu2ecxiqei4w)). Noam Rosenthal mentioned related discussions in issue 809 concerning declarative partial updates and mutation observers, suggesting potential additions like content and tag-end flags for mutation observers ([00:13:38](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ZA1AKDb9YoXD6dFgLTegj2YPUyCWmq2vbJNvyotPrQU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-aWlRM8Z_eVAXtOStBeIwCQ&tab=t.9nfap4e7n9e6#heading=h.ox90bx7n9rsy)) ([00:17:43](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ZA1AKDb9YoXD6dFgLTegj2YPUyCWmq2vbJNvyotPrQU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-aWlRM8Z_eVAXtOStBeIwCQ&tab=t.9nfap4e7n9e6#heading=h.3483tfiykukg)). The group agreed to prepare a more in-depth discussion for TAC, with Keith Cirkel and Noam Rosenthal taking on the task of shaping the agenda item ([00:20:25](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ZA1AKDb9YoXD6dFgLTegj2YPUyCWmq2vbJNvyotPrQU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-aWlRM8Z_eVAXtOStBeIwCQ&tab=t.9nfap4e7n9e6#heading=h.e04gk3nyrnqi)).
- Document Ready Promise: Keith Cirkel introduced issue 127 regarding `document.ready` as a promise that resolves when the document is ready, proposing to revive a spec previously written by Dominic ([00:21:31](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ZA1AKDb9YoXD6dFgLTegj2YPUyCWmq2vbJNvyotPrQU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-aWlRM8Z_eVAXtOStBeIwCQ&tab=t.9nfap4e7n9e6#heading=h.jmjrn82ir3dd)). Anne van Kesteren suggested starting small by focusing initially on load or DOM content loaded events, noting points raised by Dominic regarding script async and defer usages. Jake Archibald supported including multiple use cases like script async handling ([00:22:33](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ZA1AKDb9YoXD6dFgLTegj2YPUyCWmq2vbJNvyotPrQU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-aWlRM8Z_eVAXtOStBeIwCQ&tab=t.9nfap4e7n9e6#heading=h.7qnuqxt4cb8q)). Hearing no objections, Keith Cirkel agreed to move forward with refining the spec for TAC ([00:21:31](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ZA1AKDb9YoXD6dFgLTegj2YPUyCWmq2vbJNvyotPrQU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-aWlRM8Z_eVAXtOStBeIwCQ&tab=t.9nfap4e7n9e6#heading=h.jmjrn82ir3dd)) ([00:24:38](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ZA1AKDb9YoXD6dFgLTegj2YPUyCWmq2vbJNvyotPrQU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-aWlRM8Z_eVAXtOStBeIwCQ&tab=t.9nfap4e7n9e6#heading=h.651plimej512)).
- Range Values in Cross-Origin Media and Service Worker Requests: Jake Archibald raised issue 1936 to clarify whether same-origin media requests must remain special or require a cross-origin attribute to pass through a service worker when handling potential redirects ([00:25:33](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ZA1AKDb9YoXD6dFgLTegj2YPUyCWmq2vbJNvyotPrQU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-aWlRM8Z_eVAXtOStBeIwCQ&tab=t.9nfap4e7n9e6#heading=h.18twcywfci4h)). Anne van Kesteren expressed a preference for utilizing the CORS framework to avoid security edge cases, while acknowledging that either approach is secure. Jake Archibald agreed to select an approach, update the issue, and request input from Chrome networking colleagues ([00:32:55](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ZA1AKDb9YoXD6dFgLTegj2YPUyCWmq2vbJNvyotPrQU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-aWlRM8Z_eVAXtOStBeIwCQ&tab=t.9nfap4e7n9e6#heading=h.srpq2weeap0b)).
- Selected Content in Multi-Select Elements: Joey Arhar provided an update on issue 12342 concerning select multiples, noting ongoing discussions with Anne regarding whether to reuse option elements or introduce a new element. Joey Arhar and Keith Cirkel agreed that reusing option elements presents too many behavioral complications, making a new element a more sensible approach ([00:34:07](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ZA1AKDb9YoXD6dFgLTegj2YPUyCWmq2vbJNvyotPrQU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-aWlRM8Z_eVAXtOStBeIwCQ&tab=t.9nfap4e7n9e6#heading=h.d1svwbd0jcgg)). The group agreed to take the discussion to TAC ([00:35:25](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ZA1AKDb9YoXD6dFgLTegj2YPUyCWmq2vbJNvyotPrQU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-aWlRM8Z_eVAXtOStBeIwCQ&tab=t.9nfap4e7n9e6#heading=h.hr0fhi5telux)).
- Form Associated Callback Hooks and Move Before Spec: Luke discussed issue 136, highlighting discrepancies between the spec's moving steps and existing browser implementations in Firefox and Chrome regarding form ownership and form-associated callback hooks during a move before operation ([00:36:35](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ZA1AKDb9YoXD6dFgLTegj2YPUyCWmq2vbJNvyotPrQU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-aWlRM8Z_eVAXtOStBeIwCQ&tab=t.9nfap4e7n9e6#heading=h.zeggl0rofjw9)). Luke explained that implementations reset form ownership when moving controls, whereas the spec as written preserves old associations ([00:38:00](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ZA1AKDb9YoXD6dFgLTegj2YPUyCWmq2vbJNvyotPrQU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-aWlRM8Z_eVAXtOStBeIwCQ&tab=t.9nfap4e7n9e6#heading=h.rfb3zgg4rihy)). Noam Rosenthal and Mason Freed agreed that the spec should be updated to match existing implementations where moving an input between forms reassociates it ([00:39:19](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ZA1AKDb9YoXD6dFgLTegj2YPUyCWmq2vbJNvyotPrQU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-aWlRM8Z_eVAXtOStBeIwCQ&tab=t.9nfap4e7n9e6#heading=h.ubdoq0yk5f9i)). Luke agreed to write up a spec change after returning from time off ([00:42:00](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ZA1AKDb9YoXD6dFgLTegj2YPUyCWmq2vbJNvyotPrQU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-aWlRM8Z_eVAXtOStBeIwCQ&tab=t.9nfap4e7n9e6#heading=h.w746fcfunuee)).
- Focus Without User Activation: Fernando Fiori highlighted PR 11519 regarding focus without user activation, explaining that the global object capture algorithm was updated and requesting review and feedback from participants ([00:42:00](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ZA1AKDb9YoXD6dFgLTegj2YPUyCWmq2vbJNvyotPrQU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-aWlRM8Z_eVAXtOStBeIwCQ&tab=t.9nfap4e7n9e6#heading=h.w746fcfunuee)). Fernando Fiori announced plans to ship the feature in Chromium (where it is implemented behind a flag), noting successful rollout to public preview by Microsoft Teams ([00:43:18](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ZA1AKDb9YoXD6dFgLTegj2YPUyCWmq2vbJNvyotPrQU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-aWlRM8Z_eVAXtOStBeIwCQ&tab=t.9nfap4e7n9e6#heading=h.otkpsqs5qy3m)).
- Manual Elements and Menu Item Checkboxes/Radios: David provided an update on issue 11729 for manual elements, noting that checkable menu items were restructured into separate `menu item checkbox` and `menu item radio` elements based on prior feedback. Olli Pettay expressed support, noting that the syntax and event handling structures are now simplified ([00:44:34](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ZA1AKDb9YoXD6dFgLTegj2YPUyCWmq2vbJNvyotPrQU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-aWlRM8Z_eVAXtOStBeIwCQ&tab=t.9nfap4e7n9e6#heading=h.jh7qkos1crbs)). Hearing agreement, Johnny Stenback confirmed the item would move to stage three ([00:45:32](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ZA1AKDb9YoXD6dFgLTegj2YPUyCWmq2vbJNvyotPrQU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-aWlRM8Z_eVAXtOStBeIwCQ&tab=t.9nfap4e7n9e6#heading=h.ycaixh921tft)).
- Sizes Auto and Object Fit in Responsive Images: Noam Rosenthal raised issue 1248 regarding responsive images, discussing ongoing talks with major websites like Airbnb about improving `sizes auto` and resource selection when object fit is used. Noam Rosenthal proposed using the currently unused `H` descriptor in source sets to predict the source aspect ratio in advance ([00:46:37](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ZA1AKDb9YoXD6dFgLTegj2YPUyCWmq2vbJNvyotPrQU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-aWlRM8Z_eVAXtOStBeIwCQ&tab=t.9nfap4e7n9e6#heading=h.25ahdwwhl5x2)). Philip Jägenstedt and Scott Jehl discussed how object fit impacts container content boxes and source selection ([00:48:24](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ZA1AKDb9YoXD6dFgLTegj2YPUyCWmq2vbJNvyotPrQU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-aWlRM8Z_eVAXtOStBeIwCQ&tab=t.9nfap4e7n9e6#heading=h.m5sv1jebj70j)) ([00:51:54](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ZA1AKDb9YoXD6dFgLTegj2YPUyCWmq2vbJNvyotPrQU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-aWlRM8Z_eVAXtOStBeIwCQ&tab=t.9nfap4e7n9e6#heading=h.bdhnlyjjmdpo)). Noam Rosenthal stated an intention to file a PR to gather further feedback, while Philip Jägenstedt added a brief closing highlight regarding a small API change in HTML canvas stage three items ([00:50:36](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ZA1AKDb9YoXD6dFgLTegj2YPUyCWmq2vbJNvyotPrQU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-aWlRM8Z_eVAXtOStBeIwCQ&tab=t.9nfap4e7n9e6#heading=h.6yqxkt1xa45t)) ([00:53:03](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ZA1AKDb9YoXD6dFgLTegj2YPUyCWmq2vbJNvyotPrQU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-aWlRM8Z_eVAXtOStBeIwCQ&tab=t.9nfap4e7n9e6#heading=h.av3u92lij7a)).
